texts.preamble: Da vs Lokesh Goyal on 14 May, 2018 In The Court Of Samar Vishal, Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate - Ii Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cc No. 38979/2016 Date of Institution : 14.11.2002 Date of reserving judgement : 14.05.2018 Date of pronouncement : 14.05.2018 In re: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector Department of Pfa, Govt. of Nct of Delhi A-20, Lawrence Road Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 ... Complainant versus Sh. Lokesh Goyal S/o Sh Raghubar Dayal M/s Shri Balaji Masala Store, S.No. 5, Badar Pur Market Patera, Badarpur, New Delhi. R/o 60 ft Road, Subzi Mandi, More Band Extn. Badar Pur, New Delhi ... Accused Judgment: 1. texts.facts: The present complaint is filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of the As per the complaint, on 26.09.2001 at about 4:00 pm, Food Inspector (herein after referred as FI) Shri Suniti Kumar Gupta purchased a sample of "Lal Mirch Kutti (loose)", an article of food for analysis from accused Lokesh Goyal, at M/s Shri Balaji Masala Store, S.No. 5, BadarPur Market Patera, Badarpur, New Delhi, where the said food article was found stored for sale and where accused Lokesh Goyal was found vending the article of food at the time of taking the sample. The sample consisted of approx. 600 gms of "Lal Mirch Kutti(loose)" taken from an open gunny bag bearing no label declaration. The sample was taken under the supervision/direction of Sh.S.M. Haider, SDM/LHA. The sample was taken after proper mixing with the help of clean a dry jhaba. Da vs Lokesh Goyal on 14 May, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171084310/ 1 Food inspector divided the sample then and there into three equal parts by putting it into three clean and dry glass bottles. Each bottle containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to the PFA Act, 1954 & Rules, 1955. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and wrapper of the bottles containing the sample. Notice in Form VI was given to accused Lokesh Goyal and the price of sample was also paid to him vide vendor receipt dated 26.09.2001. Panchnama too was prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by the Food Inspector were signed by accused Lokesh Goyal and by the other witness Sh. S.B. Sharma, FA. Before taking the sample efforts were made to get the public witnesses to join the proceedings but none came forward, as such Sh. S.B. Sharma, FA was joined as witness. 3. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA Code Number DA vs Lokesh Goyal SMH/LHA/4663 was sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact condition and two counterparts were deposited with LHA in intact condition. Public Analyst analysed the sample and found to be adulterated being non-conforming to standards as laid down under PFA Act and Rules. The report of Public Analyst is as follows: "The sample is adulterated because it contains abundance of foreign starches and insect infested with large no of insects." Presence of large number of insect makes the sample injurious to health. As per the report of PA there were eighteen living and four dead insects in the whole of the sample. 4. Also the vendor was selling the sample commodity in an open gunny bag i.e. loose/unpacked condition which is not allowed in Delhi as per clause 24 of Rule 49 of PFA Rules, 1955. 5. It is the case of the complainant that accused Lokesh Goyal was the vendor-cum-partner of M/s Shri Balaji Masala Store, S.No. 5, Badar Pur Market Patera, Badarpur, New Delhi at the time of taking sampling as such found to be incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the above said shop. 6. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 14.11.2002 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(f)&(l) of PFA Act, and Rule 49(24) of PFA Rules, 1955 as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused. DA vs Lokesh Goyal 7. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 14.11.2002. On the basis of PA report as well as evidence led in pre-charge evidence, charge was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a) PFA Act being violation of 2(ia)(f)&(l) of PFA Act, 1954 and 49(24) of PFA Rules, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Da vs Lokesh Goyal on 14 May, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171084310/ 2 8. At the trial, the prosecution examined three witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 SDM/LHA Sh S.M. Haider, PW-2 Shri Pawan Bhagnagar, PW-3 FI Suniti Kumar Gupta. PW-3 and Sh S.B. Sharma were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh. S.M. Haider. These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample commodity of "Lal Mirch Kutti" 600 gms from the vendor for analysis, bearing no label declaration, the sample of "Lal Mirch Kutti" taken after mixing with the clean and jhaba by rotating it in all possible directions, dividing the sample into three equal parts by putting them into three separate clean and dry sample bottles, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-1/A, Notice in form VI Ex. PW-1/C, Panchnama Ex.PW-1/B. The accused furnished his statement Ex.PW1/D stating that he is the sole owner of the shop. Thereafter, DA vs Lokesh Goyal on 27.09.2001 one counterpart of the sample along with one copy of memo in form VII and another copy of memo in form VII in sealed deposited with PA vide receipt Ex.PW1/F. The remaining two counter parts of the sample in intact condition along with two copies of memo of Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited with LHA vide LHA Receipt Ex.PW1/E under intimation that one counterpart of the same has already been deposited with PA. Thereafter, on receipt of the PA report Ex.PW1/G according to which sample was found adulterated. Thereafter on completion of the investigation, the complete file was put before the Director PFA, who after going through the case file, applied his mind and gave his consent for prosecution Ex.PW1/H against the accused. Thereafter the present complaint Ex.PW1/J was filed before the Court. Then the intimation letter Ex.PW1/K alongwith copy of PA was sent to accused vide postal receipt Ex.PW1/L. During investigation, PW-3 sent a letter Ex. PW2/A to STO Ward No. 94 and received its reply stating that no such firm found registered with Sales Tax. He also sent letter Ex.PW2/C to vendor and letter Ex.PW2/B DHO, MCD but no reply was received. These witnesses were duly cross- examined by Ld. Defence Counsel. 9. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC was recorded wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. The accused chooses not to lead defence evidence accordingly the matter was fixed for final arguments.
texts.arguments: 14. In State of Maharastra vs Jathala Devshi & Ors relied upon by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Delhi Administration vs Sunil Kumar in Crl.A 59/2006 dated 28.01.2014, it was held that - "Mr. Ganatra rightly urges that there must be evidence to show that these insects were present on the date the sample was taken. He contends that if living larvae were visible to the naked eye of the analyst, the Food Inspector who collected the sample on 09.01.1973, ought to have also seen them and in as much as he has made no such note, the DA vs Lokesh Goyal report would be insufficient to hold that such insects were present when the sample was collected." 15. It was further observed in the case of DA vs Sunil Kumar (supra) that - "In (1975), 1 FAC 281 in Mukund Lal vs State where a sample of maggajkddu remained unexamined and unalyaysed for 12 to 13 days it was held that there was a possibility that the sample become infested with insects during that period.
